title: One director exchange kernel: the live route and the simulator run the same code
deviations_from_card: Critic revision applied: instrument.ts added to the write set; directorVersion() hashes voice/director-exchange.ts (exported DIRECTOR_VERSION_FILES plus a transform test seam), acceptance case 8 = one byte of the kernel changes the version. The kernel also covers client-event persistence (a dedicated case). The kernel returns {response, outcome, state} so runDirectorStep still answers exactly the DirectorResponse projection (a parity-test assertion pins the wire keys). clampClientAt moved into the kernel and is re-exported from director-step.ts. Shrunk the write set: engine.ts untouched (SimExchangeResult shape kept). Code landed as ONE refactor commit containing its tests rather than a separate test commit, because the test file imports the new module and could not be committed green on its own; the doc landed alone under the shared-surface lock. Case 6 (no source pins, one heartbeat declaration imported by useDirector.ts and clock.ts) is itself a repo scan in director-exchange.test.ts. Case 7: director-route.test.ts 13/13 unchanged. The acceptance 'directive' in case 2 uses a seeded b1-begun store at minute 9 (a fresh store at minute 30 decides nothing).
notes: Gate exits: tsc exit 2 ONLY on foreign paths (slot B's then-uncommitted runner.test.ts, analyze/profile sibling files, kpi-sim/ tree); zero errors in voice/, interview-sim/, _components/voice. Full npm run test:unit exit 0; lint:ts-ratchet 0; docs:check 0. test:perf exit 1 on three lines: job-ingest.ts 402/400 (known), app/page.tsx 8678/8664 KB and app/api/jds/generate/route.ts 3024/3023 KB - NOT mine: jds/generate's graph contains none of my changed files, and my net byte delta on page.tsx's graph (call-observations.ts +302, useDirector.ts -339) is -37 bytes; the growth comes from sibling builders' uncommitted analyze/profile files. Tool-call test helpers use fresh callIds: a repeated callId is a REPLAY answered from the record (a trap for anyone writing kernel tests). Any tool that pins directorVersion values from earlier dumps will now see a new version (intended: the kernel joined the identity).
